### Frame Material Specifications

**Material:** 
Pella Impervia products are made from Duracast material – Pella's five-layer, engineered fiberglass composite


**Thermal Properties:** 
Withstands high heat and subzero cold. Duracast fiberglass composite resists warping in summer and becoming brittle during winter


**Construction Quality:** 
Secured with corner locks, metal fasteners and injected with sealant for added strength, security and reliable water performance


**Temperature Resistance:** 
Tested from -40ºF to 180ºF, our fiberglass is engineered to withstand subzero cold, the most extreme heat and the rigorous performance requirements of a commercial building


### Hardware and Security Features

**Locking System:** 
Pella's cam-action lock pulls the sashes against the weatherstripping on single-hung, double-hung and sliding


**Operation:** 
Sashes tilt in so you can clean both the interior and exterior of the glass from inside your home


### Finish and Color Options

**Powder-Coat Finish:** 
Our long-lasting powder-coat finish resists chipping and fading and meets AAMA 624, which is a highly-rated fiberglass finish that will never need to be repainted or refinished


**Color Options:** 
Available prefinished in your choice of White, Tan, Morning Sky Gray, Brown or Black. Optional dual-color frame – White interior with a Tan, Morning Sky Gray, Brown or Black exterior

## 4. RED FINDINGS / SAFETY CONCERNS

### Active CPSC Recalls - Product Not Affected

**Casement Window Recall (2024):** 
Pella Recalls Casement Windows Due to Injury Hazard. Consumers should keep the recalled casement windows shut and locked at all times and contact Pella to receive a free repair by a Pella-designated service technician
 - Does NOT affect Impervia double-hung series

**Battery Ingestion Recall (2025):** 
Pella Recalls Sliding Patio Doors and Windows Due to Battery Ingestion Hazard. The recalled products violate the mandatory federal regulations for consumer products containing button cell or coin batteries. The Pella Reserve and Pella Lifestyle sliding doors with Insynctive technology, models 2-panel, 3-panel, and 4-panel sliding doors
 - Does NOT affect standard Impervia DH

## 7. FIELD SOURCE OPINIONS

### Mixed Professional Sentiment

**Installation Quality Concerns:** 
They were happy I didn't buy all Pella windows -- those had a lot of bowing in the frames and the plastic flanges just slide right off, so were difficult to install and needed a lot of shimming to give the appearance of being square with the window trim
 [INSTALL-CONFOUND: MEDIUM]

**Consumer Experience - Positive:** 
We had our new Pella Impervia's installed on this past Friday and I am very impressed with the Windows. The open very easily, the installers did a great job with the install


**Consumer Experience - Mixed:** 
I swapped out my old windows for Impervia about two winters ago. Honestly, they've been pretty great at keeping the chill out—my heating bills actually dropped noticeably. Fiberglass frames seem to handle temperature swings really well without warping or letting drafts sneak through


**Professional Builder Assessment:** 
I've installed quite a few of both Lifestyle and Impervia windows. Impervia, on the other hand, is pretty much set-and-forget thanks to fiberglass durability. I've seen them hold up impressively well in some brutal weather (think Wisconsin winters, ice storms, and all that fun stuff...)


**Critical Professional Opinion:** 
Someone recommended the Pella Impervia to me. For a premium window, I didn't like what appeared to be PVC beads on the outside on the display model. Also, the Impervia's thermal performance is average at best. I stayed away from Pella as I had heard terrible stories about their customer service


**Field Consensus:** Mixed sentiment with positive durability feedback balanced against installation challenges and customer service concerns. Some professionals prefer alternatives (Marvin, Alpen).
